dialogues.jp: この家には魔法使いが住んでいた。
dialogues.en: A witch used to live in this house.
dialogues.text: A witch used to live in this house.

dialogues.jp:
別にボロ家ではないけれど、新しくもない、た
しかに妖怪でも住んでいそうな日本家屋。
dialogues.en:
The house isn't exactly shabby, but isn't new either. There
could be a ghost living in this old Japanese house.
dialogues.text:
The house isn't exactly shabby, but isn't new either. There
could be a ghost living in this old Japanese house.

dialogues.jp:
子供の頃、登下校のたびに、俺はついその家を
垣根の隙間から覗き込んでいた。
dialogues.en:
I used to look over the hedge into the house on the way to
school.
dialogues.text:
I used to look over the hedge into the house on the way to
school.

dialogues.jp:
建物に興味があったのではない。その家には広
い庭があって、日当たりのよい縁側でいつも１
人のばあちゃんが白い猫を抱いて座っていた。
dialogues.en:
I wasn't interested in the building itself, but rather the
old lady who used to sit on the porch in the sun, holding a
white cat.
dialogues.text:
I wasn't interested in the building itself, but rather the
old lady who used to sit on the porch in the sun, holding a
white cat.

dialogues.jp:
ばあちゃんは遠い国からやってきた人で、髪が
金色で、瞳が青かった。
dialogues.en:
The old lady was a foreigner, with blonde hair and blue
eyes.
dialogues.text:
The old lady was a foreigner, with blonde hair and blue
eyes.

dialogues.jp:
だが、印象に残っているのはそんな外見ではな
く――いつも幸せそうな笑顔だった。
dialogues.en:
What always sticks out in my memory is not her appearance
but her happy face.
dialogues.text:
What always sticks out in my memory is not her appearance
but her happy face.

dialogues.jp:
実際のところ、彼女は俺の母方の祖母で、その
土地を借りていたのが俺達なのだが……まだ、
一度も話をしたことはなかった。
dialogues.en:
As a matter of fact, she's my grandmother on my mother's
side, and we were renting her house, but I never had the
chance to talk with her.
dialogues.text:
As a matter of fact, she's my grandmother on my mother's
side, and we were renting her house, but I never had the
chance to talk with her.

dialogues.jp:
ある日、いつものように家をのぞきこんでいる
と、彼女と目があってしまった。
dialogues.en: One day when I was looking into her house, I met her gaze.
dialogues.text: One day when I was looking into her house, I met her gaze.

dialogues.speaker: Old lady
dialogues.jp: 「おいで」
dialogues.en: "Come inside, dear."
dialogues.text: "Come inside, dear."

dialogues.jp: きれいな発音と、｛りゅうちょう／流暢｝な日本語。
dialogues.en: She spoke in clear and beautiful Japanese.
dialogues.text: She spoke in clear and beautiful Japanese.

dialogues.jp:
俺はその言葉に従って、素直に家の中に足を踏
み入れた。
dialogues.en: I did as she said and walked through the gate.
dialogues.text: I did as she said and walked through the gate.

dialogues.jp:
１本だけ植えられた桜の匂いに包まれた、あた
たかい庭だった。
dialogues.en: It was a cozy yard with the smell of cherry blossoms.
dialogues.text: It was a cozy yard with the smell of cherry blossoms.

dialogues.speaker: Old lady
dialogues.jp: 「こんにちは」
dialogues.en: "Hello!"
dialogues.text: "Hello!"

dialogues.jp: 彼女の言葉に、俺は口を動かさず頭だけ下げた。
dialogues.en: I bowed my head without saying anything.
dialogues.text: I bowed my head without saying anything.

dialogues.jp:
ばあちゃんが嫌いだったわけではないが、特に
話すこともなかったのだ。
dialogues.en: I don't mean I disliked her. I just didn't know what to say.
dialogues.text: I don't mean I disliked her. I just didn't know what to say.

dialogues.jp:
だが、彼女はそんなことは気にせず、ただニコ
ニコとしながら縁側に座っていた。
dialogues.en: She seemed carefre, she kept sitting on the porch smiling.
dialogues.text: She seemed carefre, she kept sitting on the porch smiling.

dialogues.speaker: Old lady
dialogues.jp: 「口がきけないの？」
dialogues.en: "Can you talk?"
dialogues.text: "Can you talk?"

dialogues.jp: そんなことはない。幼い俺が言った。
dialogues.en: 'Of course I can', I said like a little child.
dialogues.text: 'Of course I can', I said like a little child.

dialogues.speaker: Old lady
dialogues.jp: 「そう、それは良かった」
dialogues.en: "Good."
dialogues.text: "Good."

dialogues.jp: 彼女は白い猫を膝から庭におろす。
dialogues.en: She put down her white cat in the yard.
dialogues.text: She put down her white cat in the yard.

dialogues.jp:
猫はばあちゃんに一声鳴きかけると、そのまま
どこかに走り去ってしまった。
dialogues.en: The cat purred to grandma and ran away.
dialogues.text: The cat purred to grandma and ran away.

dialogues.speaker: Old lady
dialogues.jp: 「お菓子をあげようか？」
dialogues.en: "Do you want a snack?"
dialogues.text: "Do you want a snack?"

dialogues.jp:
彼女はそう言って、なにもない手の平を俺に向
けた。
dialogues.en: After she spoke, she showed me her empty hand.
dialogues.text: After she spoke, she showed me her empty hand.

dialogues.jp: 差し出された手にはお菓子などのっていない。
dialogues.en: There was no snack on her hand.
dialogues.text: There was no snack on her hand.

dialogues.jp:
俺の仏頂面を見てばあちゃんは悪戯っぽく笑う
と、手をゆっくりと閉じた。
dialogues.en:
Grandma grinned teasingly, looking at my sulky face, and
then closed her hand slowly.
dialogues.text:
Grandma grinned teasingly, looking at my sulky face, and
then closed her hand slowly.

dialogues.jp:
そして、再び開いた手には小さなお饅頭がのっ
ていた。
dialogues.en:
She opened her hand, and this time I saw a small steamed
bean-jam bun there.
dialogues.text:
She opened her hand, and this time I saw a small steamed
bean-jam bun there.

dialogues.jp: 手品？
dialogues.en: Magic?
dialogues.text: Magic?

dialogues.jp: そう、俺は思った。
dialogues.en: I thought it was.
dialogues.text: I thought it was.

dialogues.speaker: Old lady
dialogues.jp: 「手品じゃないわ」
dialogues.en: "It's not magic."
dialogues.text: "It's not magic."

dialogues.jp:
彼女は答え、そして、人目を気にするように前
かがみになると、唇に指をあてて微笑む。
dialogues.en:
After she said that, she leaned forward as if to prevent
anyone else hearing, and then smiled with her finger on her
lips.
dialogues.text:
After she said that, she leaned forward as if to prevent
anyone else hearing, and then smiled with her finger on her
lips.

dialogues.speaker: Old lady
dialogues.jp: 「約束は守れる？」
dialogues.en: "Can you keep a promise?"
dialogues.text: "Can you keep a promise?"

dialogues.jp: 分からない。
dialogues.en: I don't know.
dialogues.text: I don't know.

dialogues.jp: どんな約束か分からないと、約束できない。
dialogues.en: I can't make any promise until I know what it is.
dialogues.text: I can't make any promise until I know what it is.

dialogues.jp:
その答えに、だが、ばあちゃんは嬉しそうに笑っ
た。
dialogues.en: Grandma smiled with my answer in satisfaction.
dialogues.text: Grandma smiled with my answer in satisfaction.

dialogues.speaker: Old lady
dialogues.jp:
「あなたは約束の大切さを知っているから、特
　別に教えてあげるわ。お母さんにも内緒よ？」
dialogues.en:
"I know you understand the importance of the promise. So I
will tell you this, but don't tell your mom!"
dialogues.text:
"I know you understand the importance of the promise. So I
will tell you this, but don't tell your mom!"

dialogues.jp: 耳元で。
dialogues.en: I listened.
dialogues.text: I listened.

dialogues.speaker: Old lady
dialogues.jp: 「わたしは魔法使いなの。正確には魔女ね」
dialogues.en: "I am a magician. To be precise, I am a witch."
dialogues.text: "I am a magician. To be precise, I am a witch."

dialogues.jp: 魔法使い……。
dialogues.en: A witch...
dialogues.text: A witch...

dialogues.jp:
黒い帽子と、黒いコートと、黒い猫が頭に浮か
ぶ。
dialogues.en: I imagined a black hat, a black coat and a black cat.
dialogues.text: I imagined a black hat, a black coat and a black cat.

dialogues.jp:
そのどれもがばあちゃんには当てはまらなかっ
た。
dialogues.en: None of them could fit my image of grandma at all.
dialogues.text: None of them could fit my image of grandma at all.

dialogues.speaker: Old lady
dialogues.jp: 「猫ならいたでしょ。白いけど」
dialogues.en: "You saw my cat, didn't you? It is white, though."
dialogues.text: "You saw my cat, didn't you? It is white, though."

dialogues.jp:
冗談めいて笑いながら、彼女は俺の手に饅頭を
のせる。
dialogues.en:
Laughing playfully, she put a steamed bean-jam bun on my
hand.
dialogues.text:
Laughing playfully, she put a steamed bean-jam bun on my
hand.

dialogues.jp:
それは本物みたいな感触で――やっぱり本物だっ
た。
dialogues.en: It felt real -- or rather, it was.
dialogues.text: It felt real -- or rather, it was.

dialogues.jp:
どうして、魔法使いがこんなところに住んでる
の？
dialogues.en: Why does a witch live here?
dialogues.text: Why does a witch live here?

dialogues.jp: 縁側に座って、俺は言った。
dialogues.en: I asked her, sitting on the porch.
dialogues.text: I asked her, sitting on the porch.

dialogues.speaker: Old lady
dialogues.jp: 「それは恋をしたからよ」
dialogues.en: "Because I fell in love with somebody."
dialogues.text: "Because I fell in love with somebody."

dialogues.jp:
頬を桜色に染めて、今までで一番きれいにばあ
ちゃんは笑った。
dialogues.en:
Grandma blushed and gave the most beautiful smile I've ever
seen.
dialogues.text:
Grandma blushed and gave the most beautiful smile I've ever
seen.

dialogues.jp: でも、その言葉の意味はよく分からない。
dialogues.en: But I really didn't know what she meant.
dialogues.text: But I really didn't know what she meant.

dialogues.jp: だから僕は首をふった。
dialogues.en: So, I shook my head.
dialogues.text: So, I shook my head.

dialogues.speaker: Old lady
dialogues.jp: 「そうね……夢が叶ってしまったことと……」
dialogues.en: "Well, my dream came true and..."
dialogues.text: "Well, my dream came true and..."

dialogues.jp:
ばあちゃんは、饅頭のつまった俺の頬をおさえ
て笑う。
dialogues.en:
Grandma laughs, pressing a finger against my bun-filled
cheek.
dialogues.text:
Grandma laughs, pressing a finger against my bun-filled
cheek.

dialogues.speaker: Old lady
dialogues.jp: 「たぶん、日本のお菓子が美味し過ぎたのよ」
dialogues.en: "I guess I loved Japanese snacks too much."
dialogues.text: "I guess I loved Japanese snacks too much."

dialogues.jp: 今、ばあちゃんはいない。
dialogues.en: Grandma's gone now.
dialogues.text: Grandma's gone now.

dialogues.jp:
どこかへ引越したのではなく、もうこの世にい
ない。
dialogues.en:
She didn't move house, but she's gone forever from this
life.
dialogues.text:
She didn't move house, but she's gone forever from this
life.

dialogues.jp:
ただ、この家に、和菓子の好きな魔法使いが住
んでいたことは事実だ。
dialogues.en:
The fact is, a witch who loved Japanese snacks lived in this
house.
dialogues.text:
The fact is, a witch who loved Japanese snacks lived in this
house.

dialogues.jp: なぜなら――。
dialogues.en: Because...
dialogues.text: Because...

dialogues.jp: 俺にもその血が流れているからだ。
dialogues.en: I have the same blood in my veins.
dialogues.text: I have the same blood in my veins.

dialogues.jp: ◆遠い日の魔法◆
dialogues.en: ◆The magic in the past◆
dialogues.text: ◆The magic in the past◆

dialogues.jp: それは、ばあちゃんの――魔法使いの夢
dialogues.en: A dream about my grandma -- I mean a witch.
dialogues.text: A dream about my grandma -- I mean a witch.

dialogues.jp:
俺の隣の家に住んでいたばあちゃんが、俺に自
分が魔法使いであると打ち明けてくれる。
dialogues.en:
My grandma used to live next door, and told me that she was
a witch.
dialogues.text:
My grandma used to live next door, and told me that she was
a witch.

dialogues.jp:
和菓子が好きで日本に来たこと。なにもないと
ころから和菓子を出せること。
dialogues.en:
She came to Japan because she loved Japanese snacks, and she
can make them appear from nowhere.
dialogues.text:
She came to Japan because she loved Japanese snacks, and she
can make them appear from nowhere.

dialogues.jp: そして、恋をして魔法を失ったこと。
dialogues.en:
And she lost the rest of her magic power after she fell in
love with somebody.
dialogues.text:
And she lost the rest of her magic power after she fell in
love with somebody.
